title: Your own loneliness
hookLine: Jesus was alone in Gethsemane too
tomorrow: Jesus knew he'd raise Lazarus. so why did he cry?

cards: A full room can be the loneliest place there is: everyone talking, nobody asking how you are.
On the night before he dies, Jesus walks out to a garden called Gethsemane, and he takes three friends further in with him, Peter, James and John.

He tells them, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "My soul is sorrowful even unto death: stay you here, and watch with me." Then he goes on a little way, falls on his face, and prays. When he comes back, they're asleep.

teach.b: So why bring them? Matthew's answer is right there: watch with me. Jesus doesn't ask them to fix anything or find the right words.
He asks for company in the dark: not a speech, not a plan, just someone awake nearby. And they sleep. This is the same evening Peter promised he'd die with Jesus before he'd ever deny him.

teach.h: COULD YOU NOT WATCH ONE HOUR?
teach.b: He wakes Peter: "What? Could you not watch one hour with me?"
Three times he goes off to pray, and three times he comes back to find them sleeping. Matthew doesn't smooth it over. The loneliness is real, even for him, even with friends a few steps away.
One to tell a friend: Catholics have answered that question with an hour.
Some keep a holy hour of prayer, a practice linked to those words, and on Holy Thursday night the Church keeps watch after the evening Mass, staying with him in the garden.
So the lonely night isn't hidden at the edge of the story. It sits near the center, and he has been there first, face to the ground.

how: Some Catholics keep a holy hour of prayer before the Blessed Sacrament, and on Holy Thursday night parishes keep watch after the evening Mass of the Lord's Supper, remembering Gethsemane.

o: choosing time alone to rest and recharge
a sign that you've drifted far away from God
the ache of being unaccompanied, known by Jesus too

p: an hour of prayer kept in reply

s: Matthew says Jesus found his friends asleep three times
three times he came back from prayer, and three times they were sleeping.
the Gospel hides Jesus's sorrow in the garden
my soul is sorrowful even unto death: Matthew says it plainly.
Jesus took all of his disciples with him to pray alone
he took three further in, Peter, James and John, then went on a little way.

games.q: you're one of the three in the garden. it's late, you're exhausted, and he's gone a little way off to pray. what has he asked of you?
o: stay awake and watch with him.
find the right words to comfort him.
go and bring the others back.
games.why: stay you here, and watch with me. he asks for presence, not answers, and they fall asleep.

practice: Take the posture of the garden. Kneel if you can, or sit and let your head bow toward your knees, hands open, and feel the floor take your weight. Let whatever is lonely in you be there, without explaining it or rushing it off.
If you pray, you can bring it as it is, to the one who asked his friends to stay; if not, simply stay with it, the way he asked them to.

wordCard.voice: Your own loneliness. The ache of feeling unaccompanied, which the Gospel places in Gethsemane, with Jesus himself. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: stay awake, keep watch. what Jesus asks in the garden: watch with me.

carryVoice: Your line: not alone in it. Jesus knew that garden, and that sleeping circle of friends, before you did. Go gently.

sources.q: My soul is sorrowful even unto death: stay you here, and watch with me.
What? Could you not watch one hour with me?

sources.ref: Roman Missal, Holy Thursday: Mass of the Lord's Supper, transfer of the Holy Eucharist and adoration
